subject: jazz
title: Four-rung context ladder (offload+clear 0.50 / warn 0.70 / LLM-compact 0.80 / trim 0.95) applied cheapest-first, with per-rung telemetry
one_why: Trim is explicitly demoted to a floor keyed to 0.95 of the model window with a comment documenting the bug its old constant caused (trim preempting compaction and rewriting the cacheable prefix every turn); the clear rung persists large tool bodies to disk and can be delegated to a plugin keep/truncate/drop decision that falls back deterministically and never deletes a message.

subject: jazz
title: Every pressure nudge is an ephemeral request-only suffix; the prompt-cache breakpoint targets the last persisted message so nudges never move the cached prefix
one_why: Budget/context warnings exist on many agents but are persisted into history, spending tokens exactly when scarce and getting summarized into the compaction they warned about; jazz also adds a post-compaction counter-nudge that reverses its own wrap-up advice once space is freed, and accounts attachment aging-out as exactly one cache miss.

subject: jazz
title: Meltdown window measures uniqueness on name:arguments, plus a second mechanism: byte-identical read-only calls collapsed inside a single batch before anything executes
one_why: Composite-key uniqueness keeps alternating productive tools (search->fetch->search-new-query) from tripping the 40% threshold, and in-batch dedupe catches the same-turn triple-read that a cross-turn window can only notice after paying for it; dedupe is gated on declared riskLevel read-only because two identical mutating calls may legitimately be two effects; the recovery message's placement invariant (after results, never between call and result) is directly tested.

subject: jazz
title: Capability boundary enforced at execution, not prompt: no effective tool set = refuse, hidden execute-half tools refused when the model names them, refusal returned as a model-actionable tool result
one_why: Mutating tools are approval pairs (proposal + hidden execute half the model cannot call directly), 'always approve' is re-checked at dequeue so parallel grants apply, picker approvals are never auto-approved even under yolo, and the whole boundary has ~10 property tests including the adversarial 'model names the hidden tool directly' case.

subject: jazz
title: Single-token LLM command-risk classifier for execute_command with 8s/16-token budget, fail-closed to high-risk, overridable by a plugin hook that is denied escalation authority
one_why: Only an exact 'read-only'/'low-risk' token lowers risk; timeouts, errors and ambiguity stay high-risk; conversation evidence is withheld when the approver isn't the conversation author (bot bridges); the docs explicitly bound the plugin hook - it can lower a verdict but cannot expand the tool set, override allowlists, the tier, or the shell denylist.

subject: jazz
title: Parking: a run blocked on approval persists transcript + pending tool calls + TTL as a durable record answerable from another process, and resume finishes the parked tool call before iterating
one_why: Multi-surface reality (bot, webhook, unattended) means the approver is often in a different process; parking refuses to fire mid multi-call batch because replaying siblings would repeat their effects, failed turns hand their transcript to the caller before unwinding, and a parked run's tool call stays unanswered so resume is exactly-once - integration-tested across the process boundary.

subject: jazz
title: External doors (peers, webhooks) share one authorization model: a disclosure tier intersects the toolset down, and anything riskier than read-only must be named per caller
one_why: Because enforcement is toolset intersection rather than runtime approval, an injected payload at an external door is never even offered a way out - and the read-what-you-may-learn axis (none/public/internal/private) is kept deliberately separate from the may-act axis so raising disclosure cannot silently grant mutation; no other corpus subject models peer/webhook entry this way.

subject: jazz
title: Strong eval harness (pass@1/Pass^k, A/B attribution, cost guardrails, ambient-LSP and memory-journey acceptance tasks) is not wired into any CI workflow
evidence: evals/runner.ts:19-42; evals/README.md; .github/workflows/ci.yml (no evals step); grep of all workflows for 'evals' returns nothing
one_why: The harness already isolates a private JAZZ_HOME per rollout and gates cost, so a nightly scheduled job on the free-model SUT would catch harness regressions the unit tests cannot; this is the one rung separating jazz's verification from the anchors' observed ceiling of 8.

subject: jazz
title: ask_peer forces the outbound question through a single string parameter and types the reply as a quotation, not a fact
one_why: The egress control is structural: a model left to compose a request volunteers calendar/personal context into a body nobody reads, so the parameter shape is the whole reason this is a tool rather than an http_request; the reply gets web_fetch-grade framing because 'Sam's agent says X' and 'X' are different claims.
